messages:
maria: Heads-up — Customer 'PineVault' reported a spike of 502/504s on streaming /v1/chat/completions around 10:12 UTC. Started right after we rolled the new authz rate-limiter on canary. Trace IDs: trace=trc_0a1b2c3d, trc_0a1b2c4e. Short logs below.

support-bot: ALERT: gateway_502 rate increased to 2.7% in us-west1 for hosted-api (auto-notify).

jamal: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and a few raw envoy/upstream errors? Also tenant id and sample request size.

maria: Tenant: pinevault-prod, typical request is streaming chat ~ tokens=~350, keepalive long (client expects streaming). Repro curl (works locally):
```bash
curl -v --http2 -H \"Authorization: Bearer <tok>\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  --data '{\"model\":\"open-elm-13b\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"long streaming test\"}] }' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions
```

maria: snippet from edge logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T10:12:21Z] id=trc_0a1b2c3d upstream_timeout after 30000ms route=/v1/chat/completions tenant=pinevault-prod code=502 cause=upstream_response_timed_out
[2026-03-17T10:12:22Z] id=trc_0a1b2c4e connection_reset_by_peer tenant=pinevault-prod proto=h2
```

eli: Repro idea: try with --http2 and set `Connection: keep-alive` and stream a larger prompt to reproduce long-lived KV cache warmup. I suspect the new authz introduces per-tenant request queuing + a blocking DB call under load. That could push requests past envoy route timeout.

sre-kate: Checked envoy dashboards: upstream_active_requests spiked from 6 -> 120 for that tenant behind a specific mid-proxy pool at 10:11:30. Envoy error type is upstream response timeout, not 503, and we see H2 RST_STREAM for some streams.

eng-runtime-andy: Did the runtime change batching or introduce any sync calls on startup? We did a tiny kernel change last week but it was model-side only. If authz added blocking, runtime might not be able to service queued KV cache warmups.

jamal: Short mitigation: we can add a temporary route header to bypass new authz for the affected tenant(s) while we investigate. Add header X-Auth-Route: legacy-auth for pinevault-prod via support proxy rule. That typically drops authz latency. Can we apply?

maria: Applying patch to support proxy now for pinevault-prod -> adding header override. Will monitor. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

(5m later)
maria: mitigation applied. Error rate for tenant dropped to 0.3% in the 10:18 window. Client confirmed stability. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime-andy: Good hold. We still need root cause. Can we capture authz service traces for the time window? If authz per-tenant DB calls are the culprit, we need to either improve their concurrency or introduce async handoff.

sre-kate: Collected authz traces — average latency jumped from 18ms -> 1.2s for a subset of tokens due to a new per-tenant lock in permissions cache refresh. Under burst that created a fanout queue on the auth path. Envoy timeout is 30s, but the backlog plus streaming model cold start meant some upstreams hit the 30s threshold (and h2 streams get reset earlier).

jamal: Proposed immediate steps: 1) keep header bypass for affected tenants, 2) revert rate-limiter canary rollout (it introduced the lock), 3) add soft concurrency limits and async refresh for the cache. Can we commit 1) and 2) now?

maria: Done for step 1. Eng runtime has approved rollback of the canary to last stable at 10:25 UTC — rolling back now.

(after rollback)
maria: Rollback complete at 10:27 UTC. Error spike abated across regions. Customer confirmed stream stability.

eng-runtime-andy: Follow-ups: create a postmortem to document the per-tenant lock behaviour, add a canary checklist for authz changes (load test with streaming workloads), and add an observability alert that correlates tenant-level active_request spikes with authz latency.

sre-kate: I'll open the incident ticket and attach traces + config diffs. We should also consider increasing mid-proxy upstream idle timeout slightly to avoid premature resets during transient cold starts, but only after we fix the authz lock.

jamal: Repro notes for docs: use the curl above with --http2 and a ~300–500 token streaming prompt, then hit rapid parallelism (20 concurrent) for the same tenant while authz is in canary mode. Expect upstream_timeout / RST_STREAM in edge logs.

maria: Thanks team. I'll notify PineVault and schedule a postmortem sync with eng-auth and eng-runtime tomorrow.
